correctness.rationale: The proof starts from exact level means and a nonnegative-series scalar reduction. The scalar power-shift ratio is a convex combination of strictly decreasing Hurwitz-tail ratios; strict log-convexity follows from an explicit positive Laplace integral and Cauchy-Schwarz. Homogeneous tree level counting supplies the sharp operator bound and completely characterizes equality; a finite-level projection bound plus weakly null normalized radial basis vectors give matching essential norms. The tail integral test proves the coefficient, and the spectral-radius formula proves ordinary and essential radii. The packaged check.py ran 2418 supplementary finite tests. Scope: integers b>=2,m>=1; 1<p<infinity; any nonzero constant complex λ. No unproved numerical or infinite enumeration step is needed.

value.rationale: Determines the entire exact power-norm and essential-power-norm profiles, all extremizers, and a sharp polynomial critical growth coefficient for a canonical regular-tree instance of recently studied Cesàro-space dynamics. In the critical mixing regime, all Calkin norms stay one while ordinary power norms diverge at an explicitly determined rate; this quantifies finite-level amplification versus asymptotic behavior. These are natural operator invariants directly motivated by the new tree-shift class, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a basis-norm restatement.
